title: EPOC nonequilibrium TDA-DFT and full TD-DFT absorption
summary: Two explicit singlet response models on an equilibrated RKS solvent reference: TDA-DFT or coupled X/Y TD-DFT. Only optical polarization responds to the transition; the ground-state slow field remains frozen. Locally qualified on HF/6-31G with B3LYP and PBE against independently assembled A/B matrices and vacuum limits.
gates: explicit TDA-DFT or full TD-DFT selection; no automatic TDA substitution
explicit RKS functional, Gaussian basis, static and optical dielectric constants
equilibrated ground-state SCF/solvent reference and independent polarization work check
frozen ground-state slow polarization; optical derivative in the LR electronic kernel only
converged positive singlet response roots with X/Y metric normalization and finite oscillator strengths
AO transition densities are not excited-state diagonal densities; no state-specific excited relaxation claim
single-geometry root labels; APOC state/subspace matching required for continuation
explicit launch authorization; one process, one thread, <=80 AOs, <=6 roots, 1 GB envelope
local HF/6-31G qualification of TDA/full TD with B3LYP/PBE, independent A/B assembly and vacuum limits; no global spectral accuracy claim
coordinate_policy: Fixed Cartesian geometry and triaxial cavity; spectral degree two; analytic translated/rotated Gaussian AO moments.
backend_policy: Native EPOC optical response applied to PySCF RKS TDA or the full coupled X/Y TDDFT solver. Functional and basis are user inputs. Ground-state slow polarization remains frozen. This is LR nonequilibrium absorption, not state-specific relaxed excited-state solvation. Local numerical qualification covers HF/6-31G with B3LYP/PBE and vacuum controls; other systems retain explicit convergence, normalization and containment gates.
